title: PUMA: Seeing Inside Heat Shields
description: PUMA (Porous Microstructure Analysis) is NASA Ames software that analyzes micro-CT images of porous thermal protection materials to model microscale heat transfer and structural behavior. Heat shields like PICA are porous by design — they ablate and insulate — and PUMA predicts how they behave from their actual microstructure. It turns images into material properties.
provenance: Public record: compiled from official project documentation and published specifications. Fact-checked 2026-10-21.

title: Micro-CT: The 3D Microscope
description: Micro-CT (micro computed tomography) images a material sample in 3D at micron resolution, distinguishing solid fibers from void pores voxel by voxel. PUMA segments these volumes into phases — fiber, matrix, pore — that the physics solvers consume. The image is the ground truth the models must honor.
provenance: Public record: compiled from official project documentation and published specifications. Fact-checked 2026-10-21.

title: Porosity and What It Means
description: Porosity — the fraction of void space — controls both insulation and strength: more pores mean lower conductivity but weaker structure. PUMA measures porosity directly from segmented volumes, plus pore-size distributions and connectivity. TPS designers trade these against each other deliberately.
provenance: Public record: compiled from official project documentation and published specifications. Fact-checked 2026-10-21.

title: Effective Thermal Conductivity
description: A porous heat shield does not conduct heat like either phase alone — PUMA computes the effective conductivity of the mixture by solving heat conduction on the voxel geometry. Maxwell, series/parallel bounds, and direct numerical simulation bracket the answer. This number feeds the vehicle-level thermal model.
provenance: Public record: compiled from official project documentation and published specifications. Fact-checked 2026-10-21.

title: Permeability: Gas Through Pores
description: During entry, pyrolysis gases flow out through the pores — PUMA computes permeability from the pore network so the flow can be modeled. High permeability vents gas easily; low permeability builds pressure. Coupled with heat transfer, this is the ablation physics that keeps the shield working.
provenance: Public record: compiled from official project documentation and published specifications. Fact-checked 2026-10-21.

title: PICA: The Reference Ablator
description: PICA (Phenolic Impregnated Carbon Ablator) is the reference NASA heat-shield material — carbon fiberform impregnated with phenolic resin — flown on Stardust, MSL, and Orion test articles. PUMA-class analysis characterized its microstructure to predict flight performance. Understanding PICA means understanding porous ablators generally.
provenance: Public record: compiled from official project documentation and published specifications. Fact-checked 2026-10-21.

title: Ablation: Sacrificial Cooling
description: Ablation protects by sacrifice: the heat shield chars, pyrolyzes, and erodes, carrying heat away in the boundary layer. PUMA's microscale properties feed material-response codes that predict recession rate. The shield is designed to lose exactly enough of itself.
provenance: Public record: compiled from official project documentation and published specifications. Fact-checked 2026-10-21.

title: Mechanical Properties from Microstructure
description: PUMA also estimates stiffness and strength from the fiber network: load paths through connected fibers, stress concentrations at contacts. A shield must survive launch vibration and entry pressure, not just heat. Microstructure links the thermal and structural designs.
provenance: Public record: compiled from official project documentation and published specifications. Fact-checked 2026-10-21.

title: Tortuosity: The Crooked Path
description: Tortuosity measures how crooked the pore paths are — gas and heat diffuse slower through twisted channels than straight ones. PUMA computes it from random walks through the pore space. High tortuosity is good insulation and slow venting.
provenance: Public record: compiled from official project documentation and published specifications. Fact-checked 2026-10-21.

title: Validation: Arc-Jet Testing
description: PUMA predictions are validated against arc-jet tests — ground facilities that blast material samples with entry-like heating — plus flight data where available. Measured recession and internal temperatures must match the models. Validation is what turns analysis into flight rationale.
provenance: Public record: compiled from official project documentation and published specifications. Fact-checked 2026-10-21.

title: Multi-Phase Materials
description: Real TPS is multi-phase: fibers, resin char, virgin resin, pores — each with its own properties, evolving as heating progresses. PUMA tracks phases separately so the property models follow the material through charring. The shield at peak heating is not the shield that launched.
provenance: Public record: compiled from official project documentation and published specifications. Fact-checked 2026-10-21.

title: From Voxels to Vehicle
description: The full PUMA pipeline: image the sample, segment phases, compute effective properties, feed material-response codes, predict vehicle temperatures and recession, validate in arc-jets. Microscale truth becomes vehicle-scale margins. This is multi-scale engineering done right.
provenance: Public record: compiled from official project documentation and published specifications. Fact-checked 2026-10-21.

title: PUMA for New Materials
description: PUMA's real power is screening new TPS concepts before making full-scale articles: image a coupon, compute properties, and know whether the concept is worth pursuing. Faster material development means better shields sooner. Analysis accelerates invention.
provenance: Public record: compiled from official project documentation and published specifications. Fact-checked 2026-10-21.

title: Weaving: Engineered Porosity
description: Woven TPS takes porosity from accident to design: 3D weaves place fibers exactly where strength and insulation are needed. PUMA analyzes weave unit cells the same way it analyzes random fiberforms. Engineered microstructure is the future of heat shields.
provenance: Public record: compiled from official project documentation and published specifications. Fact-checked 2026-10-21.
